acceptance_criteria: AC-1 tests/test_orchestrator.py passes in full on a machine whose legacy state directory contains records, and SESSION_CLOSE states how that condition was created for the run.
AC-2 No production code path changed; the diff touches tests only, or tests plus a named shared fixture.
AC-3 No test was deleted, skipped, weakened or marked xfail; the test count does not fall.
AC-4 A test still asserts that the legacy state directory is read when it is the configured one.
AC-5 The machine's real legacy state directory is untouched.
AC-6 The repository privacy gate reports zero findings.

baseline.authority: docs/design/GOV_ORCH_1_SYNCHRONOUS_RUN_AND_ORCHESTRATOR_VERIFY.md (FROZEN) section 2.5 defines the state directory and keeps the pre-GOV.ORCH.1 legacy location readable for one release. This movement does not change that behaviour; it stops the test suite from depending on the machine's own copy of it.
baseline.consequence: Every movement whose validation plan runs tests/test_orchestrator.py fails verification on such a machine regardless of its own diff. One movement has already been blocked by exactly this.
baseline.observed_defect: tests/test_orchestrator.py::test_status_cli_reports_no_records_as_empty_list calls the status CLI with an explicit empty --state-dir and asserts the output is an empty list. scripts/orchestrator.py::_cmd_status, in its no --movement branch, always also reads LEGACY_STATE_DIR, which is a fixed path under the system temp directory and is not influenced by --state-dir. On any machine whose legacy directory is non-empty the test fails. Measured here: the legacy directory holds 33 records and the test fails on unmodified origin/main, before any change from any movement in flight.
baseline.sequencing: Small and self-contained; it unblocks the orchestrator lane.

invariants: Production behaviour is unchanged; only test isolation changes.
No credential, management address, device name or serial enters a tracked file.
No vendor data collection and no device contact: the standing collection gate holds.
No contract status is applied, removed or changed, and no FROZEN contract is edited.
report.merge_gate: Product Owner assistant review of the diff plus orchestrator verify.passed. The worker does not open a pull request and does not merge.
report.objective: Make the orchestrator status tests independent of whatever the machine happens to have in the legacy state directory, so a test result reflects the code under test and not the developer's temp directory.
output_contract: A test suite that passes independently of the machine's legacy state directory, with no coverage lost
SESSION_CLOSE stating how the non-empty legacy condition was created for the proving run, and any production-behaviour finding observed but deliberately not acted on

recommended_reasoning.reason: A small, precisely located test-isolation fix with an unambiguous pass condition.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law

The fix must make the tests pass on a machine whose legacy state directory is non-empty. Prove it: state in SESSION_CLOSE how you produced a non-empty legacy directory for the test run, and that the suite passed against it.
Do not empty or move the machine's real legacy directory to make a test pass. That hides the defect rather than fixing it.
Coverage may not shrink: the legacy-directory read is real behaviour and must still be asserted somewhere.
Do not open a pull request and do not merge. Commit on the lane and publish SESSION_CLOSE.
Publish SESSION_CLOSE with scripts/local_relay.py append using --report pointing at a JSON file you wrote first. Do not pass report JSON inline on the command line.
risks: Making the test pass by deleting the assertion rather than isolating the path.
Emptying the machine's real legacy directory, which hides the defect from the next machine.
Silently changing _cmd_status while fixing the test, so the production behaviour drifts under cover of a test fix.
Losing the coverage that the legacy directory is read at all.

in: tests/test_orchestrator.py: isolate every test that exercises the status CLI from the real LEGACY_STATE_DIR, by pointing it at a per-test temporary path, so no test reads a directory outside its own fixture
Audit the rest of tests/test_orchestrator.py for the same class of leak -- any test that depends on a fixed path outside its own tmp_path -- and isolate those too
Keep a test that proves the legacy directory is still read when it is the real one, so the GOV.ORCH.1 section 2.5 behaviour stays covered rather than merely disabled

If, and only if, the audit shows the production behaviour itself is wrong -- for example that an explicit --state-dir should suppress the legacy read -- report that finding in SESSION_CLOSE as a separate observation and do not change the behaviour under this movement
out: Changing _cmd_status's behaviour or any other production code path: this movement fixes test isolation, not the CLI
Deleting, skipping or weakening any test, or marking one xfail
Deleting anything from the machine's real legacy state directory
Any change outside tests/test_orchestrator.py, unless a shared fixture module is the cleaner place, in which case name it in SESSION_CLOSE
Any change under ui2/, project/, docs/design/ or relay/
Any vendor data collection or device contact

completed: Audited tests/test_orchestrator.py for status-CLI tests that depend on the machine's real LEGACY_STATE_DIR instead of a per-test tmp path.
Fixed test_status_cli_reports_no_records_as_empty_list to monkeypatch LEGACY_STATE_DIR to an empty per-test directory before calling the no-movement status CLI branch.

Fixed test_status_cli_usage_error_for_unknown_movement to monkeypatch LEGACY_STATE_DIR to an empty per-test directory before calling the record-not-found status CLI branch, closing the same class of leak even though it did not happen to fail on this machine's data.
preserved: test_status_lists_a_record_found_only_in_the_legacy_state_dir and test_status_single_movement_found_only_in_legacy_dir_is_flagged, which already monkeypatch LEGACY_STATE_DIR and continue to cover the GOV.ORCH.1 section 2.5 legacy-read behaviour (AC-4).
_cmd_status and all other production code in scripts/orchestrator.py, unchanged (AC-2).

recommended_reasoning.reason: Remaining orchestrator lane work is small, precisely scoped test/CLI fixes; no new architecture or vendor semantics involved.

unresolved_risks: Authority contradiction observed and not silently resolved: WORKER.md's own Git section and approved_task.json's requirements both say 'Do not open a pull request and do not merge; commit on the lane and publish SESSION_CLOSE,' while WORKER.md's closing boilerplate and the dispatch system-reminder instead say 'Open the pull request as usual, publish your SESSION_CLOSE, and stop.' This movement followed the explicit, itemized task requirement (no PR) and is flagging the contradiction for Product Owner resolution rather than picking a side unilaterally.

Production-behaviour finding (explicitly not acted on, per scope): the audit found no case where _cmd_status's legacy-fallback behaviour itself looks wrong; the two tests fixed here relied on the machine's real directory happening to be empty of/lack a matching id, not on a CLI defect. No production change made or recommended under this movement.

Ran the two affected tests against unmodified origin/main first: test_status_cli_reports_no_records_as_empty_list failed with the real directory's 33 records leaking into the empty-list assertion, exactly as the baseline described. After the fix, the full tests/test_orchestrator.py suite (114 tests) passed against that same unmodified real legacy directory, which still held 33 records afterward (confirmed by listing it before and after the run) -- it was never read, written or truncated by the fixed tests.
